For most U.S. household refrigerators, I recommend a 1,000–2,000 Wh (1–2 kWh) portable power station with at least 1,200–1,500 W of surge capacity. Choose closer to 2,000 Wh if you want to get through a full 24-hour outage with more confidence.

The right size depends on your refrigerator's energy use, compressor startup surge, and how long the power will be out.

What size do you need?

Short outages: 500–1,000 Wh

A few hours to shorter outages

Suitable for limited backup, depending on your fridge's energy consumption. Check startup surge carefully.

Around 1 day or less: 1,000–1,200 Wh

A good portable option for many refrigerators, though actual runtime may be under 24 hours.

Example: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 — listed at 1,070 Wh in the supplied results.

A full day or longer: 1,500–2,000+ Wh

My recommendation for more dependable household fridge backup, especially during longer outages.

Example: BLUETTI AC200L — buy from BLUETTI's official U.S. store — 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W continuous output, and 3,600 W Power Lifting. Listed at $899 before the supplied discount.

Product specifications and listed prices come from the supplied search results; check the retailer for current availability and pricing.

Three specifications to check before buying

Specification

	

What to look for




Continuous AC output

	

Typically 150–300 W or more for a fridge, with additional capacity for other appliances




Startup surge

	

Prefer at least 1,200–1,500 W; some refrigerators need more




Battery capacity

	

Around 1,000 Wh for shorter backup; 1,600–2,000 Wh or more for roughly a day

Choose a station with pure sine wave AC output and verify that its surge rating can start your particular refrigerator. Watts determine whether the fridge can start and run; watt-hours determine how long it can run.

How long will it run?

One supplied guide estimates that a typical full-size refrigerator needs approximately 1,400 Wh of station capacity for 24 hours after accounting for conversion losses and reserve capacity. Actual runtime varies considerably by refrigerator model and conditions.

Battery capacity

	

Approximate practical expectation




500 Wh

	

Several hours




1,000 Wh

	

Most of a day for some efficient fridges; potentially less




2,000 Wh

	

Around a day or longer for many fridges




3,000 Wh+

	

More reserve for extended outages

These are planning estimates, not guaranteed runtimes. Frequent door opening, warm surroundings, ice makers, and additional appliances can reduce runtime.
